div.p: An element for encoding controlled topics represented in the materials being described.

A subject element is a wrapper element used to encode an index term, using the required child element label. Terms are used to identify the topics and themes represented in the described materials. Such terms often provide useful access points to the materials, especially for corporate, government, or institutional records and may be drawn from controlled vocabularies or may be natural language terms.

subject must include at least one label element. label can be repeated within subject to include translations of the same term. Use the languageOfElement attribute to identify the language used in each label.

Associated date(s) (date, dateRange, or dateSet) and place(s) (placeName) may be included to further constrain the term's meaning. A role can be defined same as an subjectType and the relationship between the subject term and the materials being described can be specified. A descriptiveNote may be included if a fuller textual explanation is needed.
A list of subject terms may also be used with reference pointers (id and target) to enhance navigation of and access to the materials being described.

The order of child elements of subject is:
label
One of date, dateRange, or dateSet
placeName
role
relationship
descriptiveNote
